record.paper_title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II: Examples, Applications and Open Problems
record.context_brief: random models and expected stability rate
record.original_question: For random simplicial complexes or random group presentations, what is the expected homomorphism or cocycle stability rate, especially in the mid-range where positive stability would have consequences for the existence of non-sofic groups and for residual finiteness of hyperbolic groups?

evidence.quote: It is natural to ask what is the expected stability rate of a random object.

In that paper, it is proved that if the expected cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients of a random simplicial complex in the mid-range is bounded away from zero, then there are non-sofic hyperbolic groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a finite group G acting on a finite set X (typically G = S_n acting on {1,...,n}), and for a finitely presented group Γ = ⟨S | R⟩ with |S| < ∞ and |R| < ∞, a function f : S → Sym(X) is called an ε-almost homomorphism (with respect to the normalized Hamming distance d_H on Sym(X)) if
   (1/|R|) Σ_{r ∈ R} d_H(r(f), id) ≤ ε,
where r(f) denotes the evaluation of the relation r in Sym(X) using f. The presentation Γ = ⟨S | R⟩ is said to be permutation-stable with stability rate ρ(ε) if every ε-almost homomorphism f : S → Sym(X) is within Hamming distance ρ(ε) of some genuine homomorphism Γ → Sym(X), and ρ(ε) → 0 as ε → 0. A linear stability rate means ρ(ε) = O(ε).

Analogously, for a finite simplicial complex Y of dimension d, the cocycle stability rate measures how far an arbitrary 1-cochain c : Y(1) → Sym(X) (with permutation coefficients) with small coboundary norm
   ‖δc‖ := (1/|Y(2)|) Σ_{σ ∈ Y(2)} d_H((δc)(σ), id)
must be from a true 1-cocycle, in the normalized Hamming metric on Sym(X)^{Y(1)}. The cocycle Cheeger constant of Y is the infimum, over non-coboundary cochains, of the ratio ‖δc‖ / dist(c, Z^1).

Random model. Let Y(d, n, p) denote the d-dimensional Linial–Meshulam random simplicial complex on n vertices with full (d−1)-skeleton, in which each d-face is included independently with probability p. The "mid-range" refers to scales of p well above the cohomological connectivity threshold but bounded away from 1, e.g. p = c·log n / n for d = 2 with c in a fixed bounded interval.

Question. Determine, as a function of p (and n → ∞), the expected permutation-cocycle stability rate of a random 2-dimensional Linial–Meshulam complex Y(2, n, p), and the analogous expected stability rate for random group presentations in standard models (e.g. Gromov's density model). In particular, decide whether in the mid-range the expected cocycle Cheeger constant with permutation coefficients of Y(2, n, p) is bounded away from zero with high probability, which would imply the existence of non-sofic hyperbolic groups (and hence of non–residually finite hyperbolic groups).
artifact.category_tag: stability of random simplicial complexes and group presentations
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. A 2025 preprint "Cocycle stability in permutations of random simplicial complexes" (arXiv:2509.21566) explicitly proposes the probabilistic program: it shows that if random 2-dimensional Linial–Meshulam complexes in the mid-range typically have a linear cocycle stability rate (equivalently, the cocycle Cheeger constant is bounded away from zero), then non-sofic hyperbolic groups exist, resolving the sofic and residual-finiteness questions for hyperbolic groups. The expected stability rate of random complexes/presentations in this mid-range has not been determined.

status_evidence.title: Cocycle stability in permutations of random simplicial complexes
status_evidence.snippet: If, in a middle triangle density range, random complexes typically have a linear cocycle stability rate, then there exists a non-sofic hyperbolic group.
status_evidence.claim: The expected cocycle stability rate of random 2-dimensional Linial–Meshulam complexes in the mid-range is posed as an open program whose positive resolution would yield non-sofic hyperbolic groups.

status_evidence.title: Stability of Homomorphisms, Coverings and Cocycles II
status_evidence.snippet: It is natural to ask what is the expected stability rate of a random object.
status_evidence.claim: The expected stability rate for random simplicial complexes and random group presentations is listed as an open problem.
